bound: spring.servlet.multipart has 10MB limits but those do not constrain JSON; reviewed config does not set a Spring MVC JSON body max or Tomcat max-http-form-post-size equivalent; container/proxy defaults and heap size are deployment-dependent
driver: request body byte volume, concurrent request count, and regex input shape
dynamic_probe: Start default opsli-boot with capped heap and Redis/MySQL; POST large JSON bodies with benign and regex-adversarial content to /system/login and /api/v1/common/email/create-code; measure heap peak, GC, servlet worker occupancy, latency and ordinary endpoint availability. Stop before host OOM outside the isolated test.
entry: POST /opsli-boot/system/login, /opsli-boot/system/login-by-code, /opsli-boot/api/{ver}/common/email/create-code and /opsli-boot/api/{ver}/common/mobile/create-code under default permit-all configuration
impact: static evidence strongly supports externally triggerable request-local heap/CPU amplification on default anonymous JSON endpoints, but no dynamic OOM, GC death, worker exhaustion, or sustained unavailable evidence was collected
reachability: opsli.waf.enable=true, xss-filter=true, url-patterns=/*; SecurityConfig loads permit-all entries for the listed anonymous endpoints; WafConfig order=0 registers before controller logic and @Limiter method advice
retention: request-burst lifetime; multiple full-body copies and regex replacement results live until request completion and can overlap across servlet workers
source: anonymous application/json request body before controller @RequestBody parsing
static_poc: Send large application/json bodies to the anonymous endpoints; the WAF must read the whole body into a String, run XSS regex replacements, and re-create a ByteArrayInputStream before normal request processing.
title: Default WAF copies anonymous JSON request bodies into String, regex-filters them, then creates a second byte array before controller handling
